correctness.rationale: The support-function identity follows from orthogonal projection and Minkowski additivity. A strict-concavity simplex reduction proves the exact inradius and its entire normal contact set. KKT derivatives are valid away from vertices, which are excluded by a strict square-root perturbation; the unique stationary active set yields the exhaustive sorted threshold and all 2^k farthest points, including tie boundaries. The sharp isotropy inequalities and equality cases follow from a test direction and the maximum-weight bound; spherical beta integration gives mean width. A deterministic checker passed 390 profiles, face-stationarity candidate comparisons, and 136500 direct support samples; these finite checks do not prove the universal theorem.

value.rationale: The canonical coordinate-discotope family is a natural, nonpolyhedral zonoid family already studied in primary literature. Exact arbitrary-weight/dimension spherical contact sets have 2^k possible counts and a sharp Pythagorean 4-to-8 bifurcation in three dimensions. Under fixed mean width the uniform weights uniquely optimize both inscribed and enclosing Euclidean radii, a geometric roundness characterization across the full family. These are motivated natural geometric invariants and complete equality classifications, rather than a chosen finite slice or an unsupported small numerical improvement.
